end.summary:
Circle parts were named using examples such as a pizza slice for sector and a straight-cut piece for segment.
Dev stated that only the diameter passes through the centre and that diameter is twice the radius.
Radius, diameter, chord, arc, segment and sector relationships were practised through short questions.
Dev described rotational symmetry as matching after any angle of rotation, but said a circle has only two lines of reflection symmetry; this was not corrected later.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised circle vocabulary, radius–diameter relationships, and reflection and rotation symmetry with Dev. The pizza-slice and straight-cut examples helped connect sector and segment to familiar shapes, and the diameter rule was stated correctly. Dev mixed up the number of reflection-symmetry lines in a circle, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, draw a circle and several diameters in different directions, then discuss why every diameter is a line of symmetry and why the circle matches after any rotation.
